prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right choice depends on your home, budget, timeline and expectations. I can help you find the best fit. First, here’s how to pick the top company in St. Louis (or anywhere) and a quick checklist you can use when evaluating contractors.

How to find the best interior painter for you
- Decide scope: whole house vs. a few rooms, ceilings, trim, cabinets, texture work, repairs, color consultation, etc.
- Get at least 3 written estimates for the same scope so you can compare apples-to-apples.
- Check reputation: Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB, Nextdoor, and local Facebook groups. Look for recent projects and responses to complaints.
- Verify credentials: insurance (liability and workers’ comp), business license, and whether they offer a warranty/guarantee.
- Ask for references and photos of completed St. Louis-area projects similar to yours.
- Confirm prep work: Will they move/fill/repair, sand, prime? Proper prep often matters more than paint brand.
- Confirm products and final coat: brand and sheen, number of coats included.
- Get timeline and a clear payment schedule (avoid large upfront cash payments).

Questions to ask every painter
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide certificates?
- How many years have you been doing interior painting in St. Louis?
- Can I see before/after photos and references from recent local jobs?
- What prep and repairs are included? How do you handle popcorn ceilings, textured walls, or lead-based paint?
- What paint brands and sheens will you use? How many coats?
- What is the project start date and estimated completion?
- Do you offer a written warranty? What does it cover?
- How do you protect floors/furniture and clean up?

Red flags
- No formal estimate or only verbal quotes.
- Requests for large upfront cash payments.
- No proof of insurance or refusal to provide references.
- Extremely low bids with vague scope (likely cutting corners).

Cost guidance (approximate)
- Per room (average bedroom): $300–$900 depending on prep, trim and ceiling work.
- Per square foot (walls only): roughly $1.50–$4.00/ft² depending on region, complexity and paint quality.
- Trim/doors/cabinets cost extra; expect higher rates for detailed trim or high ceilings.
(These are ballpark figures—get local estimates for accuracy.)

If you want, I can:
- Recommend how to search locally (what keywords to use and which sources to trust).
- Give a short email/template you can send to painters requesting bids and the exact info to include.
- Help you shortlist painters if you tell me your ZIP code, whether the job is residential/commercial, number of rooms/sq ft, desired start time, and any special concerns.

Which would you like me to do next?
